title: Manage Overlapping Subnets Across Meraki Networks

cta.text: Bring your branch templates to a Micetro evaluation

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Manage Overlapping Subnets Across Meraki Networks".
Story: Overlapping Subnets Across Meraki Sites, Without Guesswork
Branch templates reuse the same subnets at every office. Watch BlueCat Micetro show each overlapping instance, let you separate one site to manage on its own, and bring it back. About 5 minutes.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
31 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element:
1. Your branch template reuses the same subnets at every office. Switch to the flat view so one search can find every copy of a subnet.
2. Every network is in one list. Filter to the guest subnet that all the offices share.
3. Four offices reuse the same guest subnet. Micetro shows every instance in one place, so nothing is guessed. Point at the row to reach its actions.
4. The row's menu button has appeared. Open it to look inside the overlapping range.
5. Open the range to see the instance of it that each office holds.
6. Opening an overlapping range adds an instance selector. Open it to see which office each instance belongs to.
7. Each instance is a Meraki network, and the selector names every one. Pick Oslo to see its data.
8. This is Oslo's guest network: its reservations, its clients. Open the selector again to compare with another office.
9. The same list of instances. Pick Helsinki to see how its data differs.
10. Same CIDR, different reality. Switch instance and the data switches with it. Go back to the list to take control of the overlap.
11. Back at the network list. Switch to the flat view to find the range again.
12. Filter to the shared range so we can manage its instances.
13. Hover the range row to bring up its menu.
14. Open the row menu; managing instances separately starts there.
15. You decide, not the software: isolate one site to manage it on its own. Choose Manage separately.
16. The dialog lists every instance. Start from none selected so we choose exactly which to isolate.
17. With nothing selected, pick Oslo first.
18. Oslo is selected. Add Helsinki so the two are separated together.
19. Two instances chosen. Separate them from the shared range.
20. Micetro asks for a change comment, so every change carries its reason. Save it to apply the separation.
21. A separated instance has its own range, its own IPs, its own custom properties. Next, undo it for Oslo, starting at its row.
22. Open the menu on the separated Oslo instance to find the way back.
23. Choose Reintegrate range to return Oslo to the shared range.
24. Reintegrate and the instance returns to the shared range. A Title set on a separated row is lost, as documented. Confirm to go ahead.
25. Another change comment, so the reintegration has a recorded reason. Save it to apply.
26. Oslo is back in the shared range. Now do the same for Helsinki, starting at its row.
27. Open the menu on the separated Helsinki instance.
28. Choose Reintegrate range to bring Helsinki back too.
29. Confirm the reintegration.
30. One last change comment for the record. Save it to apply.
31. Back to one range with all four instances.
Close: Overlaps are shown, never guessed: you choose which instances to isolate and which to keep together.
End with a call to action: Bring your branch templates to a Micetro evaluation.
